extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in film/pop-culture and academic philosophy (philosophy students, academics, and pop-culture scholars)
extracted.subtask_description: Organizing/evaluating contributions to a philosophy symposium devoted to a popular animated film (The Boss Baby), emphasizing scholarly rigor while welcoming interdisciplinary and nontraditional voices. Applies philosophical lenses to themes, filmmaking, and cultural impact of a widely-consumed movie.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bring philosophical and interdisciplinary voices into dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: “The First Annual Boss Baby Symposium seeks to bring philosophical and interdisciplinary voices into dialogue about the enigmatic 2017 film The Boss Baby.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions/participants should situate the film in philosophical discussion and/or draw on interdisciplinary methods; the organizers explicitly solicit voices beyond a single discipline to foster dialogue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer the question 'why are we so fascinated by this film?'
rubrics_metrics.description: The conference “represents a rigorous attempt to respond to the question: 'why are we so fascinated by this film?'”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should address the film's appeal, cultural resonance, or reasons for its continued fascination; proposals that directly engage this framing question are especially relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic rigor and precision expected of a conference
rubrics_metrics.description: “We rise to the unlikely interpretive challenge posed by The Boss Baby with the academic rigor and precision expected of a conference...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributions should meet standard scholarly expectations (clear argumentation, engagement with relevant literature/theory, methodological clarity), even while treating a non-canonical text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Welcome voices from all academic backgrounds
rubrics_metrics.description: “...but welcome voices from all academic backgrounds.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The symposium is explicitly inclusive of scholars across fields and levels; interdisciplinary and unconventional perspectives are encouraged alongside traditional philosophical work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attract people with unique ideas / originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizers hope to “attract people with unique ideas about the movie.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for novel, imaginative, or unconventional readings rather than retreads; originality of interpretation is valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worthy of analysis because of social/cultural impact
rubrics_metrics.description: “Something that’s worthy of analysis ... It’s valid because it has this direct impact on society, or it’s telling society something about itself, or it’s a product of society, or it’s a product of pop culture.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A justification for studying the film: submissions can argue that the film merits study due to its cultural ubiquity, societal messages, or influence, not necessarily its ‘artistic’ status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretative complexity / 'interpretative nightmares'
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizers and participants praise the film’s conflicted messaging: “Boss Baby is so in conflict with itself… you almost can’t discern what the position of the movie is.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works that exploit the film’s ambiguity, contradictory themes, or ‘interpretative nightmares’ are encouraged; complexity and internal conflict are productive features for analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of diverse philosophical/theoretical lenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples suggested: “classic Marxist analysis… feminist analysis… phenomenological perspective… Kantian relational ethics.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should state or demonstrate which theoretical frameworks they deploy (e.g., Marxist, feminist, phenomenology, Kantian ethics) and how those frameworks illuminate aspects of the film (e.g., Baby Corp vs Puppy Corp, natality, ethics of family).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to filmmaking techniques and narrative ambiguity
rubrics_metrics.description: “From a phenomenological perspective, the way the shots in the movie effect the viewer, it’s surreal. We can’t tell what’s happening in the movie is part of Tim’s imagination or if it’s actually going on.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses that examine cinematography, shot composition, surreal presentation, and diegetic ambiguity (what is imagined vs. real) are appropriate and expected; formal filmic features are legitimate objects of philosophical analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of studying average / widely-consumed movies
rubrics_metrics.description: “The kind of average movie that people don’t think about represents the things that we consume the most… Why would we not want to sit down and have a meaningful discussion about these things?”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages proposals that justify studying mainstream or ‘average’ films on grounds that they reflect and shape popular consumption and social attitudes; cultural pervasiveness is a criterion for significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include sequel and broader franchise material
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizers list interest in The Boss Baby and its sequel Boss Baby: Family Business, which “presents even more interpretive nightmares than the first.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions can engage with the original film, its sequel, or related media (TV show, memes) to trace themes, continuities, or evolving messages across texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event logistics / virtual format
rubrics_metrics.description: “Despite the listing saying that the event would be held in Las Vegas—an in-joke for those Boss Baby real ones—the symposium will take place virtually.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical requirement for participants/submitters to expect a virtual conference format; consider media and presentation formats appropriate for online delivery.
